often and seriously of picking huckleberries, that surely I could do, and its small profits
might suffice, for my greatest skill has been to want but little, so little capital it required,
so little distraction from my wanted moods, I foolishly thought. While my acquaintances went
unhesitatingly into trade or the professions, I contemplated this occupation as most like theirs,

dispose of them, so to keep the flocks of Admetus. I also dreamed that I might gather the wild herbs

in messages from heaven, the whole curse of trade attaches to the business.
